items.description: "Fix jq (contains(["delete"]))" — the Jenkins destroy guard fails on every plan action that deletes a prd VM, including Terraform's default replace ordering ["delete","create"], which it misses today (support/iac-agent/bin/check-protected-vms.sh:30-34 matches only ["delete"] and ["create","delete"]).

"extend protection (srvvault1-3+)" — as ruled (D1, 2026-09-14): the guard fails on any delete or replace of any prd VM, with no name list, in all three jobs that run it. Today each passes the single name srviac: Jenkinsfile.iac-on-push:47, Jenkinsfile.iac-apply:73, Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:181.

The apply job stays the operator's tool for creating and removing VMs, with no guard override (F1 ruling). After a VM is destroyed on Proxmox, the guard lets through the plan that recreates it. Once its vms.tf entry is gone, the guard also lets through the plan that deletes its non-VM companions, such as its DNS reservation (terraform/modules/managed-vm/main.tf:39).

"add prevent_destroy" — as ruled (D1): prevent_destroy is on the VM resource in the shared managed-vm module (terraform/modules/managed-vm/main.tf:52, lifecycle block at :208). That covers every prd VM, with no module split and no state move, so a plan that would destroy or replace any prd VM fails, in Jenkins or locally. terraform/scratch is unaffected.
Landing the slice's Terraform change alters no VM: the first terraform/prd plan after the push (iac-on-push) proposes no change caused by it.

"zero prevent_destroy despite decisions.md:512-513 claiming it" — AnsibleSpecs decisions.md's guard doctrine (now :575-576, which claims prevent_destroy on srviac and each srvvaultN) states the rails that exist after this slice and the destroy-on-Proxmox-first path they impose. Its guidance that rebuilds a prd VM by Terraform replace (:52, :236, :482, :571) follows.

"checked plan ≠ applied plan" / "single iac invocation applying the saved plan" — iac-apply plans, runs the guard and applies that saved plan inside one iac invocation, in one stage. The plan file never leaves the container, and a guard failure applies nothing. Today Jenkinsfile.iac-apply:60-77 plans and checks, then :79-90 re-plans and applies in a fresh container (:10-11). Live proof is one operator run of iac-apply.

"drop `|| true` in drift job" — the drift job no longer swallows the guard's result (Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:181), and a protected-VM hit names itself in the build description instead of reading as ordinary drift.

Runbooks that use terraform apply -replace on prd VMs switch to destroy-on-Proxmox-first (D1 ruling). That covers OpenBao single-node and whole-cluster recovery (docs/runbooks/openbao.md:98,148), the srviac rebuild (docs/runbooks/iac-agent.md:170), the cluster-member rebuild flow and its recovery notes (docs/runbooks/vm-rebuild.md:91,132-136), and the Terraform comments that direct the same (terraform/modules/managed-vm/main.tf:213,223; terraform/prd/main.tf:111). The scratch flows keep -replace (docs/runbooks/scratch-vm.md:29, docs/runbooks/vm-rebuild.md:51).

The new guard reaches the jobs only once the iac_agent role reinstalls it on srviac (support/iac-agent/install.sh:49, bind-mounted by support/iac-agent/bin/iac:50). Until then a job fails rather than passing a plan unchecked. The operator is handed the order: push, iac_agent role on srviac, iac-on-push re-run.

Destroy-on-Proxmox-first works through the apply job. A VM destroyed with qm destroy is recreated by the next apply. A VM whose vms.tf entry is removed after that destroy is forgotten, with no destroy planned for it. Owed to the operator's first real use.

"a failed SSH host-cert stage aborts iac-scheduled-certs before either leaf stage runs" — every stage of iac-scheduled-certs runs whatever an earlier stage did, and the build still goes red if any prd stage failed. Today its stages are plain declarative stages with no catchError (Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-certs:78-164).

"S4's warning about the certs job applies to the drift job too, and it is happening now rather than hypothetically" — every stage of iac-scheduled-drift runs whatever an earlier stage did, and the build still goes red if any prd stage failed. A red Terraform drift stage (Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:159) no longer skips the Ansible and CA stages.

Stage bounds in both scheduled jobs stay in shell timeouts, never a Jenkins timeout() inside catchError (Jenkinsfile.iac-apply:152-157, build #113). A powered-off srvk8sdev still skips its dev stages as UNSTABLE, without a warning.

When several stages fail, their build descriptions are combined rather than the last overwriting the others. Today certs assigns at Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-certs:91,160 while drift appends at Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:129-138. A stage that passed adds no entry, and no entry claims that a later stage did not run when it now does (certs :91).

"a dev-stage failure in iac-scheduled-certs loses its Telegram warning when a later prd stage then reds the build" — in both scheduled jobs the dev-stage warning is raised at the point the dev stage fails, once per failure, not only from post { unstable } (Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-certs:208-220, Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-drift:403-412). It therefore reaches Telegram whatever the final build result. notify.warning only writes a log marker (/work/JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/notify.groovy:46-48), and the bot raises every marker in a finished build's log (/work/DockerImages/jenkins-telegram-bot/app/bot.py:136-137,142-165).

"iac-scheduled-certs no longer sets any build description when the failure is outside its two prd stages" — closed by the D2 ruling (2026-09-14: "Don't worry about it. This is best effort.") without a code change: no fallback build description is added to either scheduled job.
